fixes.explanation: Close, but it doesn't go that way either. God says, “…a father will not bear the iniquity of his son.” (Ezekiel 18:20) Right before that, He says, “The soul who sins is the one who will die.” (Ezekiel 18:20)

That's the one, baker. The righteous man “…gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.” (Ezekiel 18:7) He sees people in need and he hands over what he has. Bread and clothing are just part of how he lives, because God's list goes on.
Power isn't who the verse names, friend. It says he “…gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.” (Ezekiel 18:7) The ones he gives to are the hungry and the naked.

That one sounds like a networking lunch, friend. The verse says he “…gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.” (Ezekiel 18:7) The people on the receiving end are the hungry and the naked. Nobody's handing out business cards here.
That's what his father did, friend. But the text says this son “…does not do likewise…” (Ezekiel 18:14) He sees the sins, considers them, and doesn't repeat them.

Offerings aren't mentioned here, friend. The text says he sees his father's sins, considers them, and “…does not do likewise…” (Ezekiel 18:14) Then it lists what he does: he doesn't look to idols, he gives his bread to the hungry, and he keeps God's ordinances (Ezekiel 18:15–17).

That would be convenient, friend. But God says the opposite: “None of the righteous acts he did will be remembered.” (Ezekiel 18:24) And “Because of the unfaithfulness and sin he has committed, he will die.” (Ezekiel 18:24)
